title: One set, one retrieval
hook: Which setup uses fewer container visits for a complete set?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that keeping each matching set together means one trip to the cupboard gets the whole set, instead of one trip to each pile

misconception: Keeping all the pillowcases in one pile and all the sheets in another is the tidiest way to store bedding.
objective: The example counts separate locations, not seconds. Keeping the chosen set’s pieces together replaces multiple location visits with one, while separating unlike sets can preserve identification.

recall.question: A bedding set's 3 pieces live in 3 different cupboards. How many places do you visit to collect one set, and how many if the set is stored together?
recall.why: Scattered, you visit each of the 3 places; kept as one set, you visit 1. This counts places, not seconds, and grouping by set helps only when the pieces are used together.
